The authors generate gauge beta functions with PyR@TE 2 and numerically solve two-loop gauge RG equations. Only the top Yukawa and Higgs quartic are additionally retained, using one-loop evolution for those couplings.

Hold the charge vector fixed, impose level matching, and set the allowed oscillator level to its minimum. This produces separate BPS and non-BPS mass branches without varying the charge or compactification moduli.

Insert a spherical charged brane into the background, determine its Euclidean turning radius, and analytically continue the saddle. The resulting trajectory tests whether electric pressure overcomes tension and carries the brane to the AdS boundary.

Reduce the theory, retain the actual infrared massless scalar sector, recompute its gauge coupling, and compare consistently normalized extremality coefficients. This distinguishes a protected compensation mechanism from simply holding the original alpha fixed.

Use a weakly tractable dual description of strong coupling, identify the projected worldsheet spectrum, and translate its mass-charge comparison through the duality dictionary. The supplied test covers singly-wound D-strings.

Tensor forecasts use Fisher methods and scaled achieved BICEP2/Keck power-spectrum covariance matrices to represent observing losses. Authors report agreement at several common parameter points with another Fisher code and a map-based code; the latter permits non-Gaussian, spatially varying foregrounds.

Multifrequency foreground cleaning is combined with patch-specific delensing: an E-mode map and a tracer of the lensing potential predict the lensing B-mode realization. The tensor forecasts allocate a separate, single-frequency, ≥6-meter telescope to this task.

For prescribed currents, the potential is first defined on δdD1 by Maxwell's equation and extended using pre-images modulo gradients. Support control and continuity are obtained through topology and advanced/retarded wave-equation Green functions.

The charged vacuum construction switches between free Maxwell smearings A0(δG) and A0(δ*G), component by connected support component, according to the sign of the Lorentz invariant square of the integrated co-primitive tensor. This introduces nonlinear dependence on g.

The vanishing argument uses compact de Rham cohomology, Poincaré duality, loop-function representatives, and the causal Poincaré lemma. Alexander duality and homological replacement reduce the relevant bilinear form to a Hopf-link configuration whose exchange conflicts with skew symmetry unless it vanishes.

Weighted level sums determine total abundance, tower fraction, and effective equation of state. Present-day abundance normalization eliminates an absolute mass parameter; parameter surveys then map mass scales, abundance distributions, and lifetime restrictions.

Boltzmann phase-space integrals determine primordial per-state abundances, expressed using modified Bessel functions and relativistic/nonrelativistic limits. Radiation- and matter-era dilution factors are followed by exponential decay factors.

For special scalar potentials admitting a scalar/flux duality, identify domain walls with charged branes and apply the WGC to their tension. Extension to generic potentials is motivational rather than established by this duality.

Compare the supersymmetric BPS lower bound with the gravitational vacuum-decay threshold; use superpotential phases and a triangle inequality to distinguish critical flat walls from higher-tension BPS walls.

Use Israel junction conditions for an instantaneously stationary spherical thin wall, with pure true-vacuum AdS inside and false-vacuum AdS-Schwarzschild outside, then expand its asymptotic mass at large radius.

Direct evolution uses fourth-order finite differences and fourth-order Runge–Kutta, enforcing ∂rψ=0 at the origin. The authors report testing an outer boundary rmax=50, where the field is about 10⁻¹⁵, against evolution in a compactified radial coordinate.

A harmonic-oscillator mode expansion and slow-amplitude averaging yield a resonant interaction system with channel i+j=k+l. Coupling coefficients are evaluated through mode-overlap integrals; their large-index behavior is investigated using Laguerre-to-Bessel asymptotics and numerical integration.

Numerical quality monitoring uses conserved norm and Hamiltonian, the virial identity, and convergence comparisons between resolutions. Global spatial refinement targets relative conservation deviations below 10⁻⁶; the authors report reliable evolution until very near collapse.

Appendix B uses Chern–Simons couplings, Poincaré duality, and holomorphic-curve arguments to assert that a supersymmetric D7 stack with nonzero relaxion coupling must intersect the NS5 cycle as point sets, even when the corresponding topological intersection number vanishes.

Dimensional reduction of fivebrane DBI and Chern–Simons actions identifies the secular potential, quantized induced D3 charge, and transverse brane KK modes. The probe action is then contrasted with the action including those charges as ten-dimensional sources.

Backreaction is expanded perturbatively in N/ND3 around a warped conifold background, using harmonic decomposition of metric and flux perturbations. Open/closed-string duality supplies a complementary interpretation through D3–D7 string threshold corrections to the gauge coupling.

Chiral block diagonalization and singular-value decomposition J=U†DV construct the modified Berry connection. Chern–Simons equations with delta-function curvature on nodal lines, Gauss linking integrals and local skein relations determine nodal-link contributions.

Adiabatic nodal-line motions are embedded in four-dimensional parameter space (t,k). Integrals of Tr(f∧f) and projected band curvature relate crossings or closed nodal-line sweeps to theta changes and first Chern numbers.
Use nilpotent-orbit Fourier support, Gelfand–Kirillov dimension bounds and supersymmetry tensorial differential equations to exclude ambiguities invisible in the perturbative expansion.

Take weak-coupling and large-circle limits together; evaluate one- and two-loop Siegel–Narain modular integrals by orbit unfolding and Poisson resummation, then promote perturbative charge sums to U-duality-covariant sums.

Represent Eisenstein series as constrained Epstein sums over invariant lattices, split solutions into graded branches, and perform Poisson resummations. The E8 lattice construction uses integral Jordan algebras and Freudenthal structures.

Imported cooling/deposition interpolation tables supply channel-dependent fc(z). Modified CLASS recombination and gas-temperature equations include hydrogen ionization, excitation and heating source terms.

Small-injection derivatives of TT, TE and EE spectra define a transfer matrix and Fisher matrix. Standard cosmological parameters are marginalized using F=Fe−Fv Fc^−1 Fv^T; diagonalization supplies orthonormal principal components in basis-model coefficient space.

Monte Python interfaced with CLASS samples the Planck low-multipole temperature/polarization, high-multipole TTTEEE and lensing likelihoods. Flat priors cover six cosmological parameters and inverse decay lifetime; chains satisfy R−1<0.01 and nuisance parameters are marginalized.

Linearize conservation equations around homogeneous equilibrium to obtain collective modes. At zero temperature, classify tensor structures under SO(1,1)×SO(2), using ideal equations and integrability identities to remove redundancies.
Use source variations and retarded linear response to obtain Kubo formulas. A Legendre transform distinguishes an imposed external electric current from the electrical current response.
Classify derivative corrections, remove redundant terms through hydrodynamic frame redefinitions, and constrain transport using local entropy production and Onsager reciprocity.

Dynamical friction is treated as gravitational Coulomb scattering of a uniform incoming scalar field past a point mass. Confluent hypergeometric solutions and momentum-flux integrals yield a drag coefficient with a finite outer-distance cutoff.

Tidal evaporation is modeled by numerical Schrödinger–Poisson solutions in a simplified spherical tidal potential, with a complex eigenvalue and an outgoing-wave boundary condition obtained using WKB.

The analysis uses nonrelativistic Schrödinger–Poisson and Madelung equations, a commutator derivation of a quantum virial identity, and numerical spherical eigenstates. Isolated eigenstates have a regular origin and wavefunction and gravitational potential approaching zero at infinity.
Use N = 1 supergravity auxiliary fields and gravity-mediated soft masses to translate quantized hidden-sector parameters into a grid of Higgs and MSSM soft terms.
Eliminate four-form field strengths algebraically to obtain a sum-of-squares axion–Higgs potential; minimize in the axion and neutral Higgs directions and track changes under integer flux jumps.
Estimate membrane nucleation with the thin-wall exponent B = 27π²T⁴/[2(ΔV)³], approximate ΔV ≃ qf0 ≃ qm²/η, and combine suppression with the conjectural upper bound on membrane tension.

Constrained instantons deform the tensionless CDL geometry by separating the two nucleation events. The constraint fixes their proper-time separation along ψ=0. These deformed geometries are off shell relative to the original CDL equations; a minisuperspace integral over their separation supplies the leading contribution.

Infinite-volume action divergences are regulated using constant transverse-size surfaces that respect de Sitter and Lorentz boost symmetries. The t0-independent reference action S0 is subtracted and its exponential absorbed into the amplitude's overall normalization.

In two dimensions, Gauss–Bonnet reduces the relevant boundary dependence to a topological contribution, leaving the volume action. In four dimensions the action includes Einstein–Hilbert, spacelike boundary, null boundary and corner terms. A half-line Fourier transform in t0 is used to isolate the contribution from linear large-time action growth.

Minimize with respect to saxions using the ρ functions as variables. For metrics given by saxion powers, the author organizes stabilized saxions as ratios of sums of products of ρ functions, reducing dependence on explicit axion polynomials.

Evaluate proper distance through ∫√Kφφ̄ dφ along displaced minima. Estimate the critical displacement by comparing inflaton-dependent ρ terms with their vacuum values; the NS example combines numerical behavior with a parametric onset estimate.
Eliminate nondynamical 3-form fields to obtain V=(Z inverse)^{ab}ρaρb+Vloc. The functions ρa contain axions and flux data, while Zab depends on saxions.

Represent toroidal Yukawa couplings by Jacobi theta functions arising from sums of open-string worldsheet instantons. Impose i+j+k≡0 mod d, with d the gcd of intersection numbers, then form linear combinations appropriate to orbifold zero modes.

Numerically vary the torus area, expand around B≈7.5, and evaluate single-field potential slow-roll parameters. The stated observable formulas are n_s=1+2η−6ε, α_s=−24ε²+16εη−2ξ and r=16ε, with derivatives taken with respect to the canonical inflaton.

Use the confined SU(2) description with mesons, effective superpotential W_eff=y_IJK Φ_K V_IJ and quantum constraint Pf(V)=Λ⁴. Select a discrete local minimum and integrate out the SUSY-breaking sector to obtain the proposed inflaton potential.

The RN discussion uses y=r−Q and an asserted freely falling trajectory y(τ)=αQ sin(τ/Q). The authors relate a brane-picture timescale to Δτ≈αΔt→0 near the horizon to motivate instantaneous decay for near-horizon observers.

A brane/flux dictionary identifies internal fluxes with their sourcing extended objects and flux tadpoles with spacetime-filling sources. This correspondence is used to transfer stability intuition between the two descriptions.

An NS5/D4 construction involving relative NS5 tilting and Seiberg duality motivates the mechanism: separated brane/anti-brane configurations decay nonperturbatively, while collision at the conformal fixed point permits perturbative annihilation through tachyonic open strings.
Impose d1=−d0=−Σ and r1=−r2=rH. The author obtains M=0, e^(2φ0)=±P/Q and rH²=Σ²∓2QP, with opposite correlated signs, and states that the remaining algebraic equations of motion are satisfied.
Use curvature components and Einstein's equations in an orthonormal frame to compute energy density and radial tension. The displayed NEC test contracts the stress tensor with k=(1,1,0,0).
Construct the bridge by replacing the exterior radial coordinate with u²=r²−r0² and joining the u<0 and u>0 descriptions. The author identifies two asymptotically Minkowski ends and a throat at u=0.

Scan Kreuzer–Skarke toric data and triangulations for the required fibration and shrinkable divisors. Use intersection polynomials, divisor Euler characteristics and cohomCalg computations to identify divisor topology and rewrite the volume.

Combine the reviewed LVS expansion with KK and winding loops and F⁴ higher-derivative terms. Compute their topological coefficients from Π_i=∫_X c₂∧D_i, canonically normalize the fibre direction, impose the stated COBE normalization and evaluate inflationary observables.

Choose sign-flip orientifold involutions and D7 configurations, determine O7/O3 loci and tadpole budgets, and compute intersection-curve genera. Winding corrections require intersections with non-contractible one-cycles; KK corrections are inferred from transverse Kähler-modulus dependence.

Apply the Gepner GSO and sector-alignment currents and the bosonic string map, then read off massless left/right little-group representations. A stochastic search constructs order 10⁸ modular invariants and groups their spectra into representative classes.

Use simple currents, their finite fusion orbits and conserved monodromy charges to construct modular-invariant matrices. Products of these matrices implement extensions; relative locality determines when matrices commute, so their ordering matters for asymmetric supersymmetry enhancement and breaking.

Interpret spectra using dimensional reduction, gauge-enhancement branches, explicit shift orbifolds and supermultiplet decompositions. Super-Higgs tests require broken gravitinos and accompanying fields to fit massive multiplets while the remainder forms allowed massless multiplets.

Hamilton–Jacobi/superpotential reduction: V=(W′)²/2−dW²/[4(d−1)], Ȧ=−W/[2(d−1)], φ̇=W′, and β=dφ/dA=−2(d−1)∂φ log W. Along radial evolution dW/du=(W′)²≥0; the holographic C-function is proportional to W^{1−d}.

Local power-series expansions and linearized deformations δW classify critical-point branches and whether they admit continuous families. Explicit exotic examples use numerical integration of chosen polynomial potentials; an inverse construction starts from φ(u) and reconstructs W and V.

Gauge-invariant linear fluctuations are reduced to one-dimensional Schrödinger problems with eigenvalue μ²=−pμpμ. Factorization into adjoint first-order operators supplies the stability argument, subject to endpoint boundary conditions.

Compute toy-model effective potentials through two loops using dimensional regularization and tadpole integration, shift the minima, and compare numerical distributions of tree-level and corrected vacuum energies.

Determine canonically normalized moduli Hessians, write the pre-uplift scalar matrix as 4e^K FFᵀ, and reduce characteristic determinants using low-rank matrix identities. Real and imaginary sectors are diagonalized separately.

Solve extrema and stability conditions for each flux choice, then construct P(Λ) by weighting vacuum energies with the input flux distributions. Dense flux ranges are approximated by continuous random variables.

Use the functional renormalization group and Wetterich equation for Γk, which incorporates fluctuations above momentum scale k. Locate interacting fixed points and diagonalize the stability matrix to classify relevant directions.

Employ a background-field metric split gμν=ḡμν+√(16πG)hμν, spinbase-invariant fermion derivatives, an Einstein–Hilbert gravitational action, the stated α=0 gauge fixing, and a Litim-type regulator adapted to fermions.

Factorize heat kernels on AdS2×S² and derive small-proper-time expansions using spectral densities, contour integration, and zeta-function sums. Charged densities require distinct intermediate- and large-black-hole expansions.

Integrate out matter using heat kernels and proper-time determinants, absorb UV divergences into flat-space counterterms, and extremize the quantum entropy function at fixed asymptotic charge. Leading corrections are evaluated at the classical saddle.

The higher-dimensional treatment solves bulk equations and IR junction conditions perturbatively in backreaction, uses singular perturbation theory to match near-brane and slowly varying regions, and dimensionally reduces to a symmetry-constrained 5D EFT. Winding-loop potentials are estimated using large-argument Bessel asymptotics.

The four-dimensional analysis treats the running deformation as a spurion, writes V(ϕ)=κ[g(ϕ)]ϕ⁴, and expands about a stationary point near a zero of κ. Matter thresholds are analyzed through their changes to κ and the dilaton-dependent Yukawa couplings.

The authors expand the D7 DBI and Chern–Simons actions in space-time derivatives, integrate over the wrapped cycle, and include ISD and IASD background fluxes. Matching the resulting scalar potential to supergravity data determines the corresponding nonstandard kinetic term.

The heavy volume modulus is integrated out at its inflaton-dependent minimum using a second-order displacement expansion and expansions in inverse αt0 and H/mt. Numerical minimization and canonical normalization supply benchmark slow-roll predictions.

Supersymmetric flux constraints DS W=DU W=0 are solved analytically in a toy model with a flat direction and numerically in a more complete flux model. Inflaton-dependent saxion values are inserted into the field-space distance integral.

The entropy argument follows semiclassical Hawking evaporation of black branes carrying discrete torsion charge. Compactifying spatial brane directions on a torus converts the flat-space case into a particle argument for the ordinary covariant entropy bound, with the stated dimensional restriction.

The de Sitter appendix interprets black-hole entropy and Coleman–De Luccia detailed balance through a conjectural finite-dimensional Hilbert space. Transitions to crunching regions are distinguished by whether the corresponding zero-CC limit admits a positive-energy theorem.

The CFT constructions use current algebra and Sugawara decomposition for an exactly marginal current-current deformation, then propose R-symmetry gauging with Chern–Simons or quantized BF couplings. Large-N counting is used to discuss induced multitrace beta functions.

Compare counterterm polynomials with CP-odd one-loop five-point string amplitudes. Lattice-orbit decompositions, trace conversions and branching rules identify contributions from massive vector multiplets and Wilson-line-induced orbifold shifts.
